Republican for Congress · WA-03
## Run a Tight Ship
Manufacturer. Citizen Legislator. Navy Captain. John Braun spent 31 years in the submarine force, built a 350-employee company in Chehalis, and led the fight against Olympia's tax surge. Now he's running to bring that same discipline to Washington, D.C.

Why John Braun
## 31 Years of Military Service
Retired Navy Captain. Six commands in the submarine force. Director of the Submarine Force Reserve Component. Three of his four children followed him into uniformed service.
## Southwest Washington Manufacturer
President of Braun Northwest — 350 employees building emergency vehicles in Chehalis since 1986. He makes payroll, meets regulations, and knows what government costs from the other side of the desk.
## Proven Record in Olympia
Senate Republican Leader. Chaired Ways & Means. Delivered the largest college tuition cuts in the nation, fully funded public education, and cut property taxes for 73% of Washingtonians.
## Stop the Tax Surge
The 2025 Legislature imposed the largest tax increase in Washington state history — nearly $12 billion in new taxes jammed through in a few weeks. Starting October 1, 2025, the sales tax expands to services that have never been taxed: advertising, IT support, security, staffing, even driver's education.
More than 90,000 small businesses must now collect and remit sales tax on services that were always exempt. Meanwhile, Democrats passed a 9.9% income tax and hiked the B&O tax on employers already barely breaking even.
"In a submarine, you don't waste space. In manufacturing, you don't waste a dollar. In government, we shouldn't waste your money either."
## Secure the Border
Complete barriers, hire agents, deploy technology, go after cartel supply chains.
## Stop Reckless Spending
Apply submarine discipline to federal budgets. Cut waste, not services.
## Lower Costs for Families
Fight inflation by cutting regulation, expanding energy, reining in government.
## Defend Manufacturing
Protect family-wage jobs, expand trade for WA agriculture, keep production in America.
## Strong National Defense
Rebuild the Navy, invest in the submarine fleet, and maintain deterrence.
## Support Law Enforcement
Back police, prosecute fentanyl dealers, protect communities from rising crime.

pages.title: Issues
pages.text:
Where I Stand
## Issues
I'm a Navy veteran, a small-business owner, and a citizen-legislator. I've balanced budgets, fought to put parents in control of schools, and I'm running for Congress to fight for working families—without becoming part of the D.C. circus.
## Cost of Living & Small Business
Families are getting crushed by inflation. I'll push for a pro-growth, pro-work agenda: cut wasteful spending that feeds inflation, reduce red tape on small manufacturers, and protect the skilled-trades economy that powers Southwest Washington. I've signed paychecks and solved real-world problems—experience I'll bring to D.C. My opponent talks press releases; I'll deliver results for paychecks and prices.
## Education: Parental Rights & College Affordability
Parents—not bureaucrats—have the right to know what's happening in their kids' classrooms. I support the Parents Bill of Rights at the federal level. In Washington, I opposed policies that cut parents out of critical decisions; my opponent voted against the House's parents' rights bill. At the state level, I authored the College Affordability Program—the largest cuts to public university tuition in the nation. College should be a ladder up, not a debt trap. I'll fight to rein in tuition costs and expand access to skilled-trades training so every young person in Southwest Washington has a path to a good career.
## Crime, Homelessness & Public Order
We can show compassion and still enforce the law. I'll pair compassion with consequences: shut down open-air drug markets, support local camping bans when shelter is available, supercharge fentanyl interdiction, and fund detox and mental-health beds. I'll make sure Southwest Washington doesn't slide into the disorder we've seen across the river.
## Secure the Border, Stop Fentanyl
I entered this race focused on border security and the fentanyl crisis. I'll complete high-priority barriers, hire and equip more agents, deploy proven technology, tighten asylum loopholes, and go after cartel supply chains. My opponent voted against the 2023 Secure the Border Act (H.R. 2). I'll vote to secure the border—because safer communities in Clark, Cowlitz, Lewis, Pacific, Skamania, and Wahkiakum depend on it.
## Salmon Recovery: Control Sea-Lion Predation
We can boost fish runs by continuing sea lion control activity. Federal law now lets states and tribes humanely remove problem sea lions on the Columbia; NOAA extended those permits. I'll secure additional funding for removal operations, hatcheries, culverts, and habitat, so fishermen see stronger returns.
## Energy Independence
Affordable energy = affordable life. I'll champion market-based production including hydropower, solar, oil, natural gas and nuclear power. The need for energy has never been greater with AI data centers and a growing population demanding ever more power. We must never go back to a time when we were dependent on foreign despots for our energy needs.
## Veterans & National Defense
As a retired Navy officer, I know readiness matters. I'll support a lethal, modern force, care for veterans with faster access to care and benefits and rebuild the industrial base—especially small manufacturers—so America never fights short of parts or people.
## Gun Rights & Hunting Heritage
I will defend the Second Amendment and Washington's hunting traditions. In my legislative races I opposed Olympia's 2023 rifle ban because it punishes the law-abiding and doesn't target criminals. In Congress I'll protect the constitutional rights of responsible gun owners and sportsmen.
## Fair Play: Protect Women's Sports
Girls deserve a level playing field. I support federal protections like the House-passed Protection of Women and Girls in Sports Act (2023) and similar 2025 legislation. My opponent opposed the 2023 bill; I'll vote to keep women's sports based on biological sex, consistent with Title IX's original purpose.
